tool.name: LineNetworkRules
tool.summary: Checks a line network (roads, pipes, rivers, cables) in one run and writes one error point per problem: dangles (free line ends), pseudo-nodes (two lines meeting end to end that could be merged), T-misses (a free end that stops just short of another line), end points that only join through a chain of near points wider than the snap tolerance (WIDE_NODE_CLUSTER), and point features (valves, hydrants) that are not on a line or not on a line end. Optionally writes a copy of the lines with a connected-component ID. Designed for a Basic licence.

param.name: snap_tolerance_m
param.dialogReference: End points closer than or equal to this many metres are the same node. Also the distance used for exempt points and point rules. 0 = only identical coordinates. Rule of thumb (not measured): 0.05 m for surveyed data, 0.5 m for scraped or hand-digitised data; the default 0.001 m is very strict. 0, or 0.000000001 m to 10,000,000 m.

param.name: checks
param.dialogReference: Checks to run: DANGLE, PSEUDO_NODE, COMPONENTS, T_MISS (needs T Distance), POINT_RULE (needs Rule Points).

param.name: pseudo_node_fields
param.dialogReference: Optional fields that must be equal on both lines for a pseudo-node to be reported (for example road class and name). Empty = every pseudo-node is reported.

param.name: t_distance_m
param.dialogReference: T_MISS: report dangles within this many metres of another line. 0 = off. A line no longer than this distance is not reported against a line it already meets at its other end. 0, or 0.000000001 m to 10,000,000 m.

param.name: dangle_exempt_points
param.dialogReference: Optional points where a free line end is expected (for example hydrants or outfalls). Used by DANGLE and T_MISS only; ignored, with a warning, when neither is checked.

param.name: rule_points
param.dialogReference: Optional points (for example valves) checked with the Point Rule.

param.name: point_rule
param.dialogReference: ON_LINE: each rule point must be on a line. ON_ENDPOINT: each rule point must be on a line end.

param.name: out_errors
param.dialogReference: Output point feature class: RULE, LAYER, SRC_OID, NODE_ID, DEGREE, VALUE, DETAIL.

param.name: out_lines
param.dialogReference: Optional copy of the lines with SRC_OID, COMPONENT_ID, COMP_LINES and COMP_LENGTH_M (plus the input attributes). An input field of one of these names is not copied (a warning says so): on an earlier line copy, its SRC_OID is replaced.

param.name: out_report
param.dialogReference: Optional Excel (.xlsx) or CSV report with Summary and Detail sheets (X and Y in the measuring system).

tool.usage:
Before you start: your lines must be split at every junction (each junction an end point of every line that meets there). A line that ends on the middle of another line is NOT connected to it: its end is reported as a DANGLE and the lines fall into different components; the run tells you how many such ends it found, also when only COMPONENTS or PSEUDO_NODE is checked. To split them: Split Line At Point needs Advanced; Feature To Line and the Planarize edit tool need Standard or Advanced; on Basic, use the Split edit tool by hand. The DANGLE row of such an end says UNSPLIT in its DETAIL ("Free end of line OID 7. UNSPLIT: it lies on line OID 12 ..."), and the run message counts these rows: select them with DETAIL LIKE '%UNSPLIT%', and the other dangles with RULE = 'DANGLE' AND DETAIL NOT LIKE '%UNSPLIT%'. Snap Tolerance: the default 0.001 m reports every gap larger than a millimetre. Rules of thumb (not measured): start with 0.05 m for surveyed or well-snapped data and 0.5 m for scraped or hand-digitised data, and look at the WIDE_NODE_CLUSTER rows.

Nodes are the end points of every line part. Interior vertices and crossings without a shared end point are NOT nodes: the network is not planarised, so two lines crossing in an X are not connected. Likewise a line that ends on the middle of another line (a T-junction where the other line is not split) is not connected to it: its end is a DANGLE marked UNSPLIT in DETAIL (and a T_MISS with VALUE 0, or at most the Snap Tolerance when the end is not exactly on the line, when T_MISS is checked), and the two lines are in different components. This differs from the topology rule Must Not Have Dangles, which accepts an end that touches another line. When your lines are not split at junctions, split them there first (every junction an end point of each line; see the licence note at the top). A line end that touches its own line (a P shape) or another part of the same multipart line is a DANGLE and is not counted as unsplit.

End points within the snap tolerance are merged transitively: a chain of end points, each within the tolerance of the next, becomes one node even if its extremes are farther apart. Such nodes are reported as WIDE_NODE_CLUSTER with their diameter in metres (VALUE; the exact largest distance between two of its end points, for any number of ends). A warning is given when the tolerance is too large for the data: a line's two different ends fall into one node while the line is at most twice the tolerance long (or its ends were chained together from farther apart than the tolerance), or the tolerance is longer than the median line part. A long, nearly closed ring whose ends are within the tolerance is simply closed, with no warning. Every test against the Snap Tolerance or the T Distance counts a distance as within it up to 1.00001 x the value (10 nanometres above a 1 mm tolerance), so floating-point noise at exactly the tolerance does not decide; a tolerance of 0 still joins identical coordinates only (a free end or rule point counts as on a line up to 0.000000001 map units away, the rounding of a computed point-to-line distance).

DANGLE: a node with one line end; not reported when a Dangle Exempt Point is within the snap tolerance. PSEUDO_NODE: exactly two different lines meet (two parts of one multipart line do not count); with Pseudo-node Fields only where all those fields are equal (null equals null; text is compared exactly, so a trailing space, another letter case or another Unicode form counts as different). The start of a single closed loop is not a pseudo-node. When the same two lines meet end to end at two nodes (a two-line ring, or two duplicate lines), each of the two PSEUDO_NODE rows names the other node instead of saying that the lines meet only there; when a third line also ends at one of the two nodes (a duplicate road with a side road, a ring with a spur), that node is not a pseudo-node, and the one PSEUDO_NODE row still names it. T_MISS (needs a T Distance above 0): a non-exempt dangle within the T Distance of another line (other parts of the same multipart line are not counted); VALUE is the gap in metres (0 means the end touches the other line, on a segment or at one of its interior vertices, but is not one of its end points). T_MISS is reported per free end: when two free ends face each other across one gap, each gets its own row. A line that already meets another line at its other end is not reported against that line when the line is no longer than the T Distance (a short stub on a road); when it is longer (a hook that comes back), the DETAIL says that the two lines already meet. POINT_RULE (needs Rule Points): ON_LINE reports points farther than the snap tolerance from every line, ON_ENDPOINT points farther than the tolerance from every line end; VALUE is the distance to the nearest one.

Components: lines sharing nodes form one component; all parts of a multipart line belong to the same component. Components are numbered 1, 2, ... by their lowest ObjectID. COMP_LENGTH_M is the total length in metres.

Distances are measured in metres in a projected system chosen from the data (the input system when it is already projected, else the matching UTM zone; for a geographic input on another datum than WGS 84, the UTM zone on its own datum when EPSG defines one (for example Ain el Abd 1970 / UTM zone 38N), else the WGS 84 UTM zone with a warning that no datum transformation is applied (older datums such as NAD27 or ED50 can then be offset by up to several hundred metres: project such data to a projected metric system first); Web Mercator family inputs (e.g. WKID 3857), which distort distances, are re-projected to the UTM zone too, and data near the poles to a polar stereographic system). The network is checked in that one system. For geographic (or Web Mercator) data wider than 3 UTM zones, polar data (beyond 84N / 80S) and input in a polar stereographic system, whose scale is not 1 over the data, COMP_LENGTH_M is measured line by line on each line's own projection (true metres), and a warning says that the Snap Tolerance, T Distance and Rule Point distances are applied in the one system. Geographic (or Web Mercator) data wider than 10 UTM zones, and lines that cannot be projected to the measuring system (or would collapse in it), stop the run with a fix: project the lines to a system suited to their extent first, or check a smaller area at a time. When the input has to be projected, the lines are first densified every 100 m in their own system, so a point on a long straight geographic segment stays on it. Error points and the line copy are written in the input coordinate system; the X and Y columns of the report are in the measuring system (its WKID is in the Summary sheet). In the line copy true curves are densified and Z/M values are dropped.

Input lines in an unknown coordinate system (for example a shapefile without a .prj) are used in their own units as if they were metres, with a warning; when every coordinate lies within -180 to 180 and -90 to 90 (longitude and latitude in degrees) the run stops: define the coordinate system first (Define Projection tool). Rule Points and Dangle Exempt Points in an unknown coordinate system (for example a shapefile without a .prj) cannot be projected: the run stops when the input has to be projected; when the input is used in its own system they are taken to be in it, with a warning. A copied field keeps its field-level domain when the output geodatabase has it, as Copy Features does (a warning names the fields that lose it); subtypes and subtype-level domains are not carried. A copied text field wider than a shapefile allows (254 characters; Pro's default length is 255) is written 254 wide to a folder output when every value fits; a longer value stops the run before anything is written. A shapefile cannot store an empty number: in a folder output empty NODE_ID, DEGREE, VALUE and COMPONENT_ID values are stored as 0 (a message says so; the RULE column tells which fields apply, and components are numbered from 1).

Selections and definition queries on all input layers are honoured. The inputs are never edited: an output or report equal to an input is refused. Tables joined to an input layer are not known by their path (a layer reports only its own table), so any output or report named like a table of a joined layer is refused, in any workspace; still, never write an output over a joined table. If an arcpy error stops the run while the outputs are written, the outputs this run created are deleted and the messages collected so far are shown before the error. A shapefile or dBASE output cuts field names to 10 bytes (about 5 Arabic letters) (COMPONENT_ID is stored as COMPONENT_); a warning names every field the output format stored under another name. SRC_OID is a Long field while every ObjectID fits 32 bits; with 64-bit ObjectIDs it is a Big Integer field in a geodatabase, a GeoPackage or the memory workspace (an ObjectID above 2^53 - 1, which ArcGIS Pro cannot store there, stops the run with the fix) and, in a shapefile, a Double field while every ObjectID has at most 12 significant digits (a dBASE Double keeps no more), else a text field of 20 characters with every digit kept; in the Excel report an ObjectID of more than 15 digits is written as text.

Not checked: two lines lying on top of each other are not reported as duplicates (a shared end where only the two lines meet shows up as a PSEUDO_NODE whose DETAIL names their other shared node), and lengths are planar metres in the measuring system, not geodesic.

Licence: every geoprocessing tool it calls (Create Feature Class, Add Field, Delete) is listed as Basic: Yes on its Esri page; use on a Basic licence is NOT VERIFIED.

Built-in alternatives: the topology rule Must Not Have Dangles needs a Standard or Advanced licence (Create Topology: Basic no); Feature Vertices To Points (DANGLE option) needs Advanced; Find Dangles and Find Disconnected Polylines are Data Reviewer checks (Standard and Data Reviewer licenses). Esri pages read 2026-11-08: Create Topology (Pro 3.5 tool page, Basic: No), Find Dangles and Find Disconnected Polylines (Pro 3.4 pages, "Available with ArcGIS Pro Standard and Data Reviewer licenses"); Feature Vertices To Points (tool page read 2026-11-07, Basic: No, Standard: No, Advanced: Yes).
